newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's May fiscal deficit $127.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's May fiscal deficit $127.5 mln.

text.p: Argentina showed a fiscal deficit in May of $127.5 million, compared with a deficit of $754 million the same month last year, the Economy Ministry announced Thursday.
The accumulated public sector shortfall for the first five months of 1997 was $1.24 billion, which was almost half the size of the shortfall for the first five months of last year.
Argentina has agreed with the International Monetary Fund on a first-half budget deficit target of $1.4 billion, to be followed by $600 million in the third quarter and $1 billion in the fourth.
The smaller deficit in May was partly due to a boost to fiscal revenues from income tax deadlines and the first tax payments by the privatized oil company YPF.

There was also a national administration shortfall of $107.4 million, a surplus run up by state-sector companies of $5.6 million, and a $25.7 million deficit transferred from the accounts of the provinces of Santiago del Estero and Catamarca.
